comparison: Both strongly support the immunofluorescence evidence for oxidized La at the cell surface (C44, C50-C52, C54). OpenEval emphasizes technical controls and TCEP validation experiments (C55-C57), while peer reviewers focus on the overall compelling nature of the conclusion. High agreement on core finding.

OpenEval R1 includes TCEP reduction experiments (C55-C57) that peer R2 implicitly accepts as part of 'multiple complementary approaches.' Both support these findings, though peer review doesn't explicitly discuss TCEP experiments separately.

Both support antibody blocking and functional experiments (C45, C60-C62). OpenEval notes TCEP's potential non-specific effects (C63), while peer reviewers emphasize the compelling nature of the fusion promotion data without raising specificity concerns. Strong agreement on main conclusions.

Both address TCEP dose-response (C63). OpenEval explicitly acknowledges potential non-specific effects, while peer reviewers accept the data as part of the rigorous complementary approaches without raising concerns about specificity.

Perfect overlap on C67-C68. Both strongly support the reduced vs. oxidized recombinant La experiments showing differential fusion and resorption activity. OpenEval provides technical details about sample size and statistics, while peer reviewers praise this as part of complementary approaches using cysteine-targeted methods.

Both strongly support cysteine mutant data (C71-C73, C75-C76). OpenEval notes the mechanism remains unclear and findings are correlative, while peer reviewers specifically praise the cysteine mutant approach as a key strength for directly tying phenotypes to oxidation targets. High agreement with OpenEval being more cautious about mechanistic interpretation.

Both support NAC experiments showing ROS-dependent regulation (C78, C81-C83). OpenEval acknowledges NAC's pleiotropic effects, while peer reviewers emphasize the convincing nature of the ROS-dependent oxidation and translocation data. Agreement on conclusions with OpenEval noting methodological caveats.

Both support qPCR control data (C79-C80) showing NAC doesn't affect differentiation markers. OpenEval treats this as an important methodological control, while peer reviewers implicitly accept it as part of the overall convincing evidence for ROS-dependent regulation.

Perfect overlap on C86-C88. Both support phosphorylation data showing ROS promotes dephosphorylation. OpenEval notes uncertainty about direct vs. indirect mechanisms, while peer reviewers accept this as strong support for the de-phosphorylation conclusion without raising mechanistic concerns.

Both strongly support rescue experiments (C89-C90, C49). OpenEval notes partial rescue suggests additional mechanisms, while peer reviewers specifically praise cysteine mutant rescue as directly tying phenotypes to oxidation. Strong agreement with OpenEval providing more nuanced interpretation of partial effects.

Both support key mechanistic conclusions about cytoplasmic oxidation (C84, C91-C92, C100). OpenEval emphasizes the logical inference that NAC blocks cytoplasmic oxidation, while peer reviewers endorse the cysteine mutant data as strong mechanistic evidence. Agreement on main conclusions.

OpenEval R9 addresses cytoplasmic oxidation mechanism (C100), while peer R10 addresses the broader mechanistic model. Both support the overall conclusion that oxidized La promotes fusion, with peer reviewers emphasizing novelty and significance.

Both address TCEP effects on La localization (C58-C59). OpenEval notes the inference about binding is speculative without direct assays, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these data as part of the complementary approaches without raising concerns about speculation.

Both strongly support the central thesis about ROS-dependent oxidation promoting fusion (C4-C5, C8-C12, C94-C95, C100, C121). OpenEval synthesizes evidence across all figures, while peer reviewers emphasize the compelling and novel nature of the mechanistic insights. Strong agreement on main conclusions.

Both address the distinction between nuclear and surface La forms (C5, C11-C12) and build on prior work. OpenEval treats this as part of the central thesis, while peer reviewers emphasize the novelty and broader significance for cell biology. Agreement on the importance of this distinction.

OpenEval R12 addresses background knowledge (C1-C3, C15-C17), while peer R11 addresses the novelty building on this background. Peer reviewers accept the foundational context and emphasize how current work advances understanding.

Both address prior work from Whitlock et al., 2023 (C18-C25, C64-C66). OpenEval treats this as established foundation, while peer reviewers accept this context and emphasize how current work provides novel mechanistic insights beyond the prior study.

Perfect overlap on C107. Both support the conclusion that La is a redox-regulated fold-switching protein. OpenEval notes detailed structural studies would strengthen the claim, while peer reviewers accept the broader significance for cell biology beyond bone. Agreement with OpenEval being more cautious about structural evidence.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic speculation about phosphatase activation (C108-C113) as uncertain. Peer reviewers do not explicitly address these speculative mechanistic claims, focusing instead on the supported conclusions.

Both address therapeutic implications (C122-C124). OpenEval rates therapeutic potential as uncertain/speculative, while peer reviewers acknowledge potential but note lack of in vivo validation reduces translational potential. Strong agreement that therapeutic claims require additional validation.

OpenEval R19 addresses therapeutic speculation (C123-C124), while peer R11 addresses the distinction between La forms that underlies therapeutic potential. Both support the existence of distinct forms, with OpenEval being more cautious about therapeutic applications.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about ROS biology (C26-C41) as supported established knowledge. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these background claims, accepting them as appropriate context.

OpenEval evaluates citations to Berndt et al. work on La structural changes (C42-C43, C77, C104-C106) as supported background. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these background claims but accept the biochemical basis they provide.

OpenEval evaluates comparative context from other protein systems (C115-C120) as supported background. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these comparative claims but implicitly accept the biological plausibility they provide.
OpenEval evaluates experimental timeline claims (C125-C126) as supported methodological context. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these timeline details.
OpenEval evaluates La sequence information (C69) as supported factual background. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate this basic protein information.
OpenEval evaluates claims about NAC's pleiotropic effects (C96-C98) as supported with appropriate caution. Peer reviewers do not explicitly address these methodological caveats about NAC specificity.
OpenEval R23 addresses rescue experiment result (C99), which overlaps with peer R9's evaluation of rescue experiments (C89-C90, C49). Both support these findings as key experimental results.

Both address main findings summary (C101-C103). OpenEval treats this as a summary of collective data, while peer reviewers emphasize the strong support and novel mechanistic insights. Agreement on core conclusions.
OpenEval evaluates surface localization confirmation (C53) as supported but not novel. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate this claim, treating it as part of the overall evidence base.

Both address La dimerization via disulfide bonds (C71). OpenEval treats this as supported by gel data and consistent with prior work, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the cysteine mutant evidence they specifically praised.

OpenEval evaluates loading control (C74) as supported methodological control. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate this technical control but implicitly accept it as part of the rigorous Western blot data.
